properties.name: Question.gap_id's declaration states why it is not a node reference
properties.rationale:
THE SWEEP GOT WIDER WHEN IT WAS RUN WITHOUT A FLOOR, and the count of kinds went from the expected three to four. The root-cause pass measured only the three properties `heal.rs` names. Re-swept 2026-08-29 across EVERY `*_id` property with no minimum-instance floor:

    TemporalFact.subject_id        334 values, 334 resolve   a NODE REFERENCE
    Snapshot.target_id             196 values, 192 resolve   a HISTORICAL ANCHOR
    Question.gap_id                 57 values,   0 resolve   a COMPUTED-FINDING REFERENCE
    Resource.dependency_graph_id      1 value,    0 resolve   a CROSS-DESIGN REFERENCE

The fourth was not in any earlier reading and is a kind nobody had named: it holds `dynograph-foundation`, which is a GRAPH id rather than a node id, and it is not a declared property at all — the store is a property bag, so it was written and never validated against anything.

⚠️ AND THREE MORE ARE DECLARED BUT HAVE NEVER BEEN WRITTEN: `ReadinessAssessment.target_id`, `DimensionAssessment.target_id`, `DimensionObservation.target_id`, all at zero instances. They read like node references — an assessment OF a node — but whether a scored node's later deletion makes the assessment wrong (a node reference) or leaves it as the surviving record of what was scored (a historical anchor) is exactly the `subject_id`-versus-`target_id` question again, and with no instances there is no evidence to settle it either way. Recorded as undecided ON PURPOSE rather than guessed, because a wrong `node_ref` on an unpopulated type would be a rule nobody could have tested.

WHY THE SCHEMA IS EDITED AND THE FLAG IS NOT. Every instinct here says "declare them and let the guard sort it out", and that is the move this change refuses. `Snapshot.target_id` MUST NOT be declared: four of its values dangle today and all four are correct — three artifacts deleted at `epoch:content-store-discontinued` and `ctr:anthony` merged into `who:ajs`. A snapshot exists to preserve what a node was, so a snapshot pointing at nothing is the mechanism working. Declaring it would make `dangling_reference` fire on correct history, which is the failure this project judges worse than no detector at all.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary:
Adding the reason to two schema property descriptions — `Snapshot.target_id` (schema/temporal.yaml) and `Question.gap_id` (schema/core.yaml) — so a reader meets the judgement at the point of the declaration rather than inferring it from an absent flag. Closes the defect named by `fact:which-properties-are-node-references-is-a-judgement-made-once-and-never-recorded-for-the-others`: `subject_id` and `target_id` are declared IDENTICALLY apart from `node_ref` and nothing said why, so the next reader either declares it and breaks history, or leaves it and never learns the omission was deliberate.

THE SCHEMA IS THE RIGHT PLACE BECAUSE IT IS SERVED. The YAML is `include_str!`d into reflow2-core and reaches agents through `describe_schema`, so a sentence here is read at the moment somebody is deciding what a property means. That is the same reasoning `dec:skills-served` applies to skills, and the same reasoning the revise-design correction applies to tool descriptions — the text an agent reads at call time is the text that governs.
